newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Q1 GDP down vs Q4 due technical factors.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Q1 GDP down vs Q4 due technical factors.

text.p: A 0.4 percent seasonally adjusted fall in Finland's first-quarter gross domestic product was mainly due to technical factors, an official at Statistics Finland (SF) said on Tuesday.
"It is mostly technical," senior statistician Erkki Laakari said by telephone.

The slowdown in GDP growth year-on-year -- to 4.0 percent in the first quarter from 5.8 percent in the fourth -- combined with the fact that fourth quarter figures have a heavier weighting than first quarter numbers and "tricky turn-of-the-year statistical methodology" caused the fall, he said.
Year-on-year growth at 4.0 percent came in below the 4.5-5.5 percent range of forecasts by 10 economists in a Reuters poll.

Output growth in industry, 3.7 percent year-on-year, was partly held back as there were four working days less in the first quarter than in the year-ago period while trade and commerce, which rose 1.6 percent, was affected by the fact that there were less shopping days, SF said in a statement.
Production rose in the first quarter in all branches of industry apart from land and water construction, it said.
"The highest increase in output in the first quarter was in building construction, which grew by over 14.5 percent compared to the corresponding period the year before," it said.

"Investments were up by just under three percent in the first quarter. Investments in the construction of residential buildings increased particularly rapidly," SF said, pointing to a 27 percent year-on-year rise.
Exports rose 9.8 percent in the first quarter while imports rose 1.9 percent.
Agriculture output rose 2.0 percent and forestry -- boosted by timber cuttings -- rose 7.8 percent. @

In manufacturing, wood and paper output rose 12.2 percent compared to a 2.4 percent decline in the fourth quarter, while output growth in the metal, engineering and electrotechnical industry slowed to 2.1 percent from 5.9 percent in the final quarter last yuear, SF said.
Transport and communication sector output rose 8.0 percent year-on-year in the first quarter.
SF said private consumption rose 2.8 percent in January-March and the wage sum grew by 0.8 percent.
